title: Incremental historical merge operator with privacy-aware resynthesis
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: implement a resilient, incremental 'merge operator' for console usage analytics that can safely reconcile historical event batches with realtime streams while performing privacy-aware resynthesis for PII-suspect records. This operator should enable resumed, partial backfills without reprocessing entire tenants and must preserve event lineage and auditability for compliance reviews. Rationale: current large-scale reprocesses are expensive, error-prone, and either overwrite audit provenance or produce duplicate records. Teams need a tooling primitive that makes replays incremental, bounded in cost, and safe for audited tenants.
proposal: Introduce a stateful merge operator that takes ordered historical shards and live stream input and emits idempotent delta writes to downstream analytics tables. Key features: 1) watermarked windows per-tenant to limit replay scope; 2) resumable resume-tokens and compact checkpoints tied to lineage IDs; 3) a schema-aware transform stage that can 'resynthesize' fields for privacy (e.g., tokenized or hashed email/SSN) based on tenant policies; 4) conflict-resolution policy (last-write-by-event-timestamp with tombstone semantics); 5) cost-aware sharding so we can target only changed partitions. The operator will expose a dry-run mode and produce deterministic verification artifacts to validate parity with source streams.
design_notes:
- Schema contract: ingest will rely on a canonical event envelope (event_id, tenant_id, origin_time, observed_time, payload, lineage_id, source_version). The transform DSL will include a small set of deterministic resynthesis functions (hash-with-salt, k-anonymize, redact, and synthetic-sample).
- Checkpointing: checkpoints are per-tenant, per-shard, and include last-applied lineage_id and a compact summary (event_count, byte_checksum).
- Lineage preservation: every output row retains a lineage_id and proof-of-origin metadata for audits.
- Performance: operator must support streaming apply with micro-batching and backpressure; aim for 10k events/sec per shard on p4d instances.
- Safety: all resynthesis operations are reversible only to the extent allowed by policy (most will be one-way). Audit logs will record which resynthesis function was applied and the salt version used.
implementation_plan:
1) Prototype operator in a staging namespace (2 sprints): create transform DSL, checkpoint proto, and simple apply engine.
2) Integration: wire to console backfill coordinator and staging Kafka topic; add dry-run verifier that emits diff reports.
3) Tenants: run smoke tests with a representative tenant and compare outputs with current reprocess job.
4) Scale testing: run end-to-end load tests with synthetic data to validate throughput and latencies.
5) Rollout: enable operator for low-risk tenants behind feature flag, observe for 2 weeks, then broader rollout.
6) Documentation and runbooks: include forensic steps to validate lineage and to abort/rollback partial runs.
rollback_plan: If discrepancies or a privacy regression are detected: 1) immediately disable operator via feature flag; 2) stop all in-flight apply jobs and mark checkpoints as 'quarantined'; 3) restore downstream tables from pre-run snapshots (snapshots taken before any production run); 4) run the dry-run verifier to identify divergence and iterate. Prioritize manual audit and stakeholder signoff before re-enabling.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic dry-run parity checks detect no more than 0% unresolved divergences for synthetic test suite
Lineage metadata is present on >99.99% of output rows for audited tenants
No duplicate events produced when operator is run twice from the same checkpoint
Resynthesis functions applied according to tenant policy and recorded in audit logs
End-to-end run for a medium-sized tenant completes within cost budget and without human intervention
progress_updates: 2026-03-10: Kickoff meeting with Analytics, Console, and Privacy. Agreed on canonical envelope shape and initial transform set.
2026-03-11: Prototype DSL evaluated; hashed-email and redact primitives implemented. Checkpoint format sketched in Confluence.

2026-03-12: Integration spike with staging Kafka done; dry-run verifier emits sample diff report. Found an edge case with reordering around late-arrival events — extended conflict-resolution doc for review.
